subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@finbot.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 Aug 2026 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a quick recap of what we covered and the proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary / pain points
- Primary business pressure: inference unit economics — margins are getting squeezed as usage scales (higher token volumes + per-token costs).
- Current stack: custom transformer hosted on AWS (SageMaker endpoints), mixed GPU types (p4d + some g4dn for burst).
- Observed metrics you shared: ~120k requests/day, avg 1.2k tokens/request, p50 latency ~320ms, occasional spikes that push p95 > 1s.
- Key constraints: need to reduce per-token cost ~30-40% without sacrificing core accuracy for NLU tasks.
- Openness to techniques: willing to try batching/caching and quantization if quality validated. Not comfortable with any approach that causes >1-2% accuracy regression on intent classification.

Success criteria (what success looks like for FinBot)
- Reduce cost per 1M tokens by ~35% (demo target)
- Maintain p50 latency <= 350ms and p95 within acceptable SLA (we can define)
- No more than 2% degradation on benchmarked intents / slot fills

What Redwood can do / initial plan
1) Run a lightweight model profiling pass (kernel-level and sequence distribution) against a small traffic sample to estimate batching/cost benefits.
2) Recommend quantization profile options and run accuracy regression checks on your benchmark prompts.
3) Propose a 2-week POC: profiling, caching pilot, and a small production canary to validate unit economics at scale.
4) Provide a preliminary cost model (attached) and a draft SOW for the POC.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Modeling.xlsx, SOC2-Share-Request.pdf

Immediate next steps
- Sofia: share a 24-72 hour traffic sample export (anonymized) and any benchmark prompts you want used for regression testing.
- Redwood: we’ll run the profiling pass and share a short findings deck + a draft POC SOW.
- Proposed tech deep-dive (30–45m) with our engineer Dev Patel next week — are you available Wed 8/12 or Thu 8/13?

Happy to adjust — want to make sure we’re aligned on risk/benefit before a formal POC.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (555) 555-1234

Marissa — thank you for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few quick items: 

- I’ll send a 72-hour traffic sample (anonymized) by EOD Monday. That will include the token counts and request IDs.
- We are open to quantization experiments but must validate on your side against our intent classification suite — agreed on the <=2% regression limit.
- For cost modeling, we’d like an initial top-line estimate (range) so procurement can see potential savings vs our current AWS spend.
- Procurement (cc’d) will look for an SOW + initial pricing bands and any standard terms we should expect.

Also attaching a small sample export in case it’s helpful: finbot_traffic_sample.csv

Sofia

sofia@finbot.ai

Looping in a quick tech note from my side — thanks Marissa for the summary.

A few initial asks so we can size the profiling work:
- Sample should include token histogram and a handful of representative long/short requests (we can ingest CSV).
- If they can provide the model type (e.g., custom 7B GPT-like, or base Llama 2 variant) and whether they use KV cache reuse (session affinity), that helps select kernels and batching expectations.

Technical approach:
1) Lightweight profiling on 72-hour sample to compute sequence length distribution and batching efficiency and estimate throughput gains with continuous batching + prefix caching.
2) Quick quantization sweep (8-bit and 4-bit PTQ) on a dev snapshot to estimate accuracy delta on their intent suite.
3) Produce a one-page table: expected tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens (current vs projected), and quality delta.

I’m available for the deep-dive Wed 8/12 10–11am PT or Thu 8/13 2–3pm PT. If either works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short tech checklist.

— Dev

Sofia — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

1) You’ll share the 72-hour anonymized traffic sample (we received the sample you attached — thank you).
2) Tech deep-dive scheduled with Dev on Wed 8/12 at 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent).

4) Draft POC SOW attached (Redwood_POC_SOW.pdf) — this outlines a 2-week POC focused on profiling, caching pilot, and limited canary.
5) We will provide an initial pricing band in the findings deck; final pricing will depend on model profile and expected throughput.

Quick ask for procurement: please review the draft SOW and flag any contractual items you need for the POC (NDA/standard MSA items, billing PO, or data-handling clauses).

We’re aiming to have the profiling results and pricing band to you by Fri 8/14 so you have something to take to procurement that week.
